beats.subline: Tuesday, November 3, 2026 close — chip stocks lifted the S&P 500 and Nasdaq while Apple's soft margin outlook weighed on the Dow, as traders awaited midterm election returns.
beats.body: AMD, Broadcom, Micron and Nvidia each gained more than 2% as chip stocks rebounded, but Apple fell nearly 2% (about $94 billion in market value) after warning that rising memory-chip costs will pressure holiday-quarter margins; oil eased on hopes of US-Iran progress even after a reported US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island, and S&P 500 futures slipped overnight as traders bet on large Democratic wins in the midterms.

beats.headline: Taiwan logs 49 Chinese aircraft in a day as 'gray zone' pressure builds ahead of local elections
beats.body: Taiwan's Defense Ministry counted 49 PLA aircraft plus six PLA Navy warships and six China Coast Guard vessels operating around the island in the 24 hours to November 3, part of a pattern analysts link to Beijing's response to Taiwan's November 28 local elections.

beats.headline: US strikes near Strait of Hormuz again as Iran calls Washington's reply 'unconvincing'
beats.body: A US official said American forces struck Iranian targets, including on Qeshm Island, after Iranian forces fired on a US jet; Trump confirmed the strikes but called the operation minor with no immediate plan to resume a broader campaign, while Iran's security council secretary Mohsen Rezaei rejected Washington's response to Tehran's conditions for reopening the strait.

beats.headline: Anthropic extends Claude's invisible text watermark to older models including Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6
beats.body: As of November 3, Anthropic applies its text watermark — a variant of Google DeepMind's SynthID-Text that survives copying and light editing — to output from Claude Mythos 5, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 on its API, with Amazon Bedrock to follow within days; the company says the mark cannot be disabled and is expanding detector access to regulators, media and researchers, though an absent mark does not prove text is human-written.
